thread:
incident-bot: Pager — p99 decode latency SLO breach on prod-cluster-usw2 (alertid=i-9834). Current p99 1.8s -> baseline 0.55s :rotating_light:

sarah.w: I'm on call. first noticed at 03:12UTC, correlates with a TRT/FlashAttention kernel rollout from earlier deploy.

mike.h: confirmed — spikes start ~03:08 after canary rolled. p95 also elevated but p99 worse. streaming stalls for long-running chat (kv cache writes hanging).

priya.k: customer-impact: two medium customers (acme-data, finok) reported UI stalls and truncated streams. telemetry shows ~12% request stream resets.

julia.t: grabbing logs, running a quick tail on node gpu-3:
```
[03:09:11] decode: step=kv_update size=512 ms=1.1
[03:09:12] decode: step=kv_update size=512 ms=1200 <-- tail
[03:09:13] trt: kernel=flash_attn_v2 launch_ms=1189
[03:09:13] nvrtc: jit cache miss, compiling kernel
[03:09:14] decode: stall waiting for kernel completion
```

nate.l: sounds like spiky JIT/compile path, maybe kernel wasn't precompiled for this variant. we rolled new TRT kernels with ldc flags yesterday.

sarah.w: immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic to fallback model variant (no flashattn) 2) roll back kernel package on affected pools 3) pin compile cache to warm images.

mike.h: routing to fallback is fastest. can we flip routing policy for the impacted customer tags?

priya.k: yes, we can set routing policy on the LB to prefer model:v1-compat for those tenants. doing whitelist for acme-data + finok.

julia.t: starting reroute now — updating routing table for prod-usw2-ml-lb: 10.0.3.21 -> model:v1-compat.
```
# command
curl -X POST https://console.api.redwood/routing/update -d '{"selector":"tenant:acme-data,finok","target":"model:v1-compat"}'
```

incident-bot: Routing update applied (changeid=r-447).

sarah.w: monitoring. frankly need quick root cause: why did kernel JIT cause 1.2s stalls?

nate.l: hypothesis: compiler flag set `-use_fast_math` + TRT flashattn change causes divergent kernels, forcing nvrtc compile per-launch on some shapes. also eviction of jit-cache after image build due to mismatch.

mike.h: checking build metadata for last deploy (deploy-bot shows):
```
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T02:58Z -> runtime:trt-kernel-2026-03-10-v2
build_meta: flags=["-O3","-unroll-loops","-use_fast_math"]
```

priya.k: customer traffic dropped to fallback — p99 trending down to 0.62s for routed tenants. other tenants still see elevated p99 ~0.9s but reduced.

julia.t: I can roll back the kernel package on the auto-scaling pool that serves model:v2. plan: rollback to trt-kernel-2026-03-01-v1. Need thumbs.

sarah.w: Do it, but coordinate with infra — we should avoid evicting hot containers. also add a temporary autoscale policy to spin up additional warm nodes to reduce JIT pressure.

nate.l: rollback started on pool gpu-pool-12. using canary-rollback script:
```
./canary-rollback --pool gpu-pool-12 --artifact trt-kernel-2026-03-01-v1 --parallel 2
```

mike.h: adding a JIT warm step on startup to precompile common shapes. patching startup hook to run a small compile matrix for seq_len [32,128,512].

julia.t: applied warmup hook to image, pushing new image to staging. will promote to prod after verification.

sarah.w: customer comms? Priya can you coordinate brief note to affected customers: acknowledge SLO breach, mitigation, ETA for full rollback.

priya.k: on it — sending short note.

priya.k: message sent to acme-data+finok: "we observed decode streaming stalls after a kernel rollout; we've routed your traffic to a compatibility model and are rolling back the kernel. we expect full restoration in ~20–30m. apologies for disruption."

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-213 — Severity 2 (service degraded). Pager silenced.

mike.h: after rollback p99 on affected nodes: 0.58s, p95 0.18s. overall prod p99 back to 0.62s. streaming reset rate down from 12% -> 0.5%.

julia.t: follow-ups: 1) add precompile CI job for TRT/FlashAttention kernels across common shapes 2) remove risky compiler flag combo from default build profiles 3) improve canary gating to include p99 metrics for streaming.

sarah.w: agree. please add tasks to eng-runtime board and assign owners. we'll keep INC-2026-213 open for postmortem and RCA.

nate.l: RCA notes (quick): root cause = kernel rollout that introduced shape-specific kernel variants + `-use_fast_math` flag causing nvrtc cache miss + per-launch JITs => tail latency. secondary: canary lacked sufficiently representative streaming traffic.

priya.k: customers restored, monitoring for 1h. I'll prepare customer post-incident summary.

sarah.w: great work. closing realtime triage. we'll transition to postmortem thread in /incidents. :white_check_mark:
